record.paper_title: Selected Old Open Problems in General Topology
record.original_question: If X is a homogeneous ω-monolithic compact space, must the cardinality of X be at most 2^ω?

evidence.quote:
A compact space X is
ω-monolithic if the closure of any countable subset of X is metrizable.

Problem 16. Is the cardinality of every homogeneous ω-monolithic compact space
X not greater than 2ω?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Call a compact Hausdorff space $X$ $\omega$-monolithic if, for every countable subset $A \subseteq X$, the closure $\overline{A}$ is metrizable. A topological space $X$ is homogeneous if for every pair of points $x, y \in X$ there exists a homeomorphism $h: X \to X$ with $h(x) = y$.

Question: Must every homogeneous $\omega$-monolithic compact Hausdorff space $X$ satisfy $|X| \le 2^{\aleph_0}$?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in surveys of selected old open problems in general topology. Known results bound the cardinality of homogeneous compacta by $2^{t(X)}$ (where $t(X)$ is tightness), but a direct affirmative answer for $\omega$-monolithic homogeneous compacta is not established in the searched literature. No solution was found.

status_evidence.title: Topological Homogeneity (Arhangel'skii and van Mill)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing cardinality questions for homogeneous compacta and related monolithicity hypotheses.
status_evidence.claim: Cardinality bounds for homogeneous compacta involving monolithicity are discussed as open.

status_evidence.title: A new bound on the cardinality of homogeneous compacta
status_evidence.snippet: Bounds the cardinality of a homogeneous compactum by 2^{t(X)}.
status_evidence.claim: Best known bound uses tightness; does not directly resolve the omega-monolithic case.
